title: Non-aborting Preview launch (`--preview-mission`)
limitation: `--test-mission` sets `AutoTest`, under which any script error, including one in harness `eval`/`exec` text (a debug-console line, a watch, a teleport, an agent snippet), closes the game with exit code 2; mission end and player death quit the process; no briefing is shown; `--no-strict` does not help because `--test-mission` itself sets `AutoTest`.
current_workaround: P1 launch `--test-mission <stage> --window --no-splash --no-strict --harness 0`, presented as a "strict preview"; generated snippets are pre-checked before sending; a tolerant console waits (DG001 option C); the positional launch without `--test-mission` is a P0 probe (DG001 option B).
proposed_feature: [launch] Add `--preview-mission <path>` (runs in place, no staging, no `AutoTest`), `--preview-briefing` (show the briefing first, like Shift+Preview) and `--preview-on-end quit|menu`; preview is treated like `AutoTest` for exit flow only, never for the script-error abort. The maintainers may prefer a mode of `--test-mission` instead (doc 08 open question 9).
hook_points: `P:Foundation/Platform/AppConfig.cpp#L668-L670` (beside `--test-mission`), `#L806-L808` (absolutise before `-C`); `P:Foundation/Platform/AppConfig.hpp#L236-L239` (getters); `R:apps/cwr/Game/GameApplication.cpp#L1697-L1735` (`StartGameMode`: resolve with `MissionPathLoader`, set `LoadFile`, skip `StageTestMissionForGame`, set a `PreviewMission` flag); `P:World/WorldImpl.cpp#L2235-L2256` (`StartIntro` branch); `P:UI/DisplayUIMenus.cpp#L2012-L2066` (new `StartPreviewMission` modelled on `StartAutoTest`), `#L966-L1007`; `P:UI/OptionsUIApp.cpp#L944-L969`; leave `P:Game/Scripting/ExpressExt.cpp#L150-L165` (the `AutoTest` abort) unchanged; tests: a Catch2 CLI-parse test beside `R:tests/unit/apps/Server/test_simulate.cpp` and a Trident mission test using `extra_args`
benefit: A debug console, watches, live tweaks, "Try it" and live shot preview that survive their own mistakes; briefing preview; Preview returns to the menu instead of quitting. Unblocks doc 31 §5.4 and §7.4 and doc 32 §4.2.
profiles_affected: Preview only, no content impact. Ce first; Cwr once ported through CE's `port` label. Cwa199 never.
status: not filed (raise in the CE #35 discussion)

title: Open a mission in the in-game editor from the command line (`--edit-mission`)
limitation: No documented way launches straight into the in-game editor with a mission. By source reading a positional `…/<name>.<Island>/mission.sqm` calls `OpenEditor()`, while a CE organisation member reports that it plays the mission instead [U].
current_workaround: Export to the user's missions folder and tell the user which clicks to make (doc 08 option 1); a P0 probe of the positional path.
proposed_feature: [launch] `--edit-mission <path>` that reuses the existing `OpenEditor()` path, after finding why CE #35 reports that it does not open the editor (one candidate: `OpenEditor()` returning early before `GWorld->Options()` exists [I]).
benefit: Round trips with the stock editor for users who also edit there; answers an open community request.
profiles_affected: Launcher only, no content impact. Ce first; Cwr if ported.

title: In-process Preview restart (`preview_restart`)
limitation: A running game cannot reload `mission.sqm` in-process; every change needs a relaunch, whose boot cost is unmeasured.
current_workaround: Relaunch for each Preview; staging keeps the project the single source of truth.
proposed_feature: [harness] A `preview_restart{path}` harness command that closes the `DisplayMission` stack on the main thread and re-runs the preview start. Unwinding the display stack safely is the risky part [I].
hook_points: `R:apps/cwr/Game/GameApplication.cpp#L556-L594` (`CreateGameHarness`), `#L1743-L1751` (`CanRemount`, the existing "safe from menu only" reasoning); the `StartPreviewMission` of ER-001
benefit: Fast edit-and-preview loops without a process boot.
profiles_affected: Preview only; needs ER-001. Ce first.
status: not filed (after ER-001, and only if the boot time measured for doc 08 OQ3 justifies it)

title: `LoadFile` declared as 256 bytes but defined as 512: test-mission paths truncated
limitation: `GameApplication.cpp` declares `extern char LoadFile[256]` while the definition is `char LoadFile[512]`, so the game's own re-staged test-mission path (`<TempDir>/mission-smoke/<16 hex>/Missions/<name>.<island>/mission.sqm`) is truncated at 255 bytes.
current_workaround: Keep staging roots and mission folder names short (doc 01 §7.2).
proposed_feature: [fix] Make the declaration match the definition (or replace the global with a bounded string type) and add a long-path test.
benefit: Previews of missions with long names or deep temporary paths no longer fail obscurely.
profiles_affected: Launcher, no content impact. Ce, then Cwr.

title: Launch path handling: positional `.pbo`, `--test-mission <file>` and silent rejections
limitation: The positional argument's help text says ".pbo or .sqm", but `StartIntro` has no `.pbo` branch; `--test-mission` given a `mission.sqm` file copies only that file, so no `<name>.<island>` folder exists and nothing starts; no exit code is set when `ProcessFullName` rejects a path [I].
current_workaround: Always pass the unpacked mission folder; the Preview supervisor watches the log with a timeout.
proposed_feature: [launch] Handle a positional `.pbo` or correct the help text; accept a `mission.sqm` path by staging its folder; exit with a documented code when a path is rejected.
benefit: Fewer silent "nothing happened" launches, for Plotroom and for players' shortcuts.
profiles_affected: Launcher, no content impact. Ce, then Cwr.

title: Test-mode boot failure keeps the game running; exit code 2 is overloaded
limitation: Without `--check`, a failed `StartAutoTest` logs that it could not boot and leaves the game running with no mission. Exit code 2 means a script error, a command-line exception or `--dev` in a release build, so only the log tells them apart, and log text is mission-controllable (ER-013).
current_workaround: A log watch plus a timeout; exit codes mapped and the log read (doc 08 §4.2).
proposed_feature: [launch] In test and preview modes, exit with a distinct, documented code when the mission cannot boot, and give command-line errors their own code.
benefit: Reliable Preview supervision and clear error messages without log scraping.
profiles_affected: Launcher, no content impact. Ce, then Cwr.

title: Campaign test launch at a chosen row with seeded campaign variables
limitation: Test launches are single-mission only: `StartAutoTest` clears every campaign variable first, and no command line starts a campaign at a chosen row or with given state; whether `--test-mission` reads a campaign `description.ext` is [I].
current_workaround: A throwaway debug campaign whose first mission is a setup router that `saveVar`s the chosen state (doc 18 §8.3); a staged `initintro.sqs` that sets the variables (doc 32 §4.3); a Preview-only prologue that shows what was assumed (doc 35 rc51).
proposed_feature: [launch] (proposal of this register [I]) `--test-campaign <dir>` with an optional start row and a variables file, entering the normal campaign path with the variables injected by the same loop as mission start.
hook_points: `P:UI/DisplayUIMenus.cpp#L2039` (clears campaign variables); `P:AI/AICenter.hpp#L555`; `P:UI/OptionsUIApp.cpp#L350-L384` (Begin), `#L458-L501` (restart from a row), `#L883-L892` (`VarSet` loop); `R:apps/cwr/Game/GameApplication.cpp#L1697-L1735`
benefit: Automated whole-campaign and branch tests (Path Explorer, doc 29 §5.3 playthrough checks) without hand-built debug campaigns.
profiles_affected: Preview only, no content impact. Ce first.
source_docs: 08 §4.2; 32 §4.3; 18 §8.3; 29 OQ2; 35 rc51; integration item I29-08 (engine side)

title: Documented, stable tooling flags
limitation: `--test-mission`, `--autotest`, `--check` and `--harness` are Dev-visibility options that appear in no help output of a release build; an official update could strip or change them, and the shipping Steam binary's behaviour is untested.
current_workaround: A capability probe at every launch; the zero-patch export fallback (doc 08 option 1).
proposed_feature: [launch] Document these flags as supported tooling options (basic help visibility or a written stability note), in line with CE #166's request to document launch options.
benefit: Editors and test tools can rely on the launch path across official updates.
status: proposed (CE #166, opened by others: launch options not documented)

title: Saves inside Preview
limitation: Save, load and autosave do not work in the stock editor's Preview (CE #166), and `StartAutoTest` deletes `continue.fps`, `autosave.fps`, `save.fps` and `weapons.cfg` before a test run, so `saveGame` checkpoints cannot be tested in a preview.
current_workaround: Checkpoint modules are validated statically; testing save and load needs a real playthrough.
proposed_feature: [launch] Let preview modes save and load into a session-scoped folder that is discarded at exit.
benefit: Checkpoint and resume behaviour becomes testable from the editor.

title: Test verbs registered by `--test-mission` and `--harness`
limitation: Either flag registers about 300 gated `tri*` verbs into the same evaluator that runs the mission's own scripts, including a debug console that runs SQF, file writes with unchecked names, profile and settings changes, MP admin commands and synthetic input (doc 24 F2).
current_workaround: The linter denies test and debug verbs in missions (doc 24 §5.2); Preview runs a staged copy; the Preview dialog says plainly that it runs the mission with the user's rights.
proposed_feature: [launch] Register test verbs only with an explicit `--test-verbs` flag that Trident passes, so Preview flags alone do not widen the mission's reach (doc 24 P2).
hook_points: `P:Game/Commands/GameStateExtTestAudio.cpp#L2990-L2994` (the gate); `R:apps/cwr/Server/ServerApplication.cpp#L171-L174`; the new flag in `P:Foundation/Platform/AppConfig.cpp` beside `--test-mission`; Trident spawn in `R:engine/Trident/src/client/instance.rs`; gate test `R:tests/unit/engine/Poseidon/Dev/Debug/test_dev_mode_gates.cpp#L43-L83`
benefit: Previewing a downloaded mission no longer hands it the test and debug toolbox.
profiles_affected: Preview and test tooling, no content impact. Ce, then Cwr.

title: UI harness commands and the `log` event
limitation: The protocol schema lists `click`, `wait_display`, `query{what:"display"}` and a `log` event, but `PoseidonGame` registers none of the three commands (their `RegisterUIQuery`/`RegisterWaitDisplay` helpers have no call site) and no emitter for `log` was found.
current_workaround: UI clicks through `exec` of the gated test verb `triClick <idc>`; display changes from `display` events; logs from `--log-file` or stdout.
proposed_feature: [harness] Register the UI query and wait commands in `PoseidonGame` (behind ER-010's capability flags) and emit the `log` event, or remove them from the schema.
benefit: Preview automation without test verbs; the schema matches the binary.

title: Structured script-error and mission-end events
limitation: Preview results are read from exit codes and log lines (`Script error at`, `AUTO-TEST SUCCESS`, `HARNESS_PORT=`), but missions control log text (`logInfo`, `textLog`, `debugLog`) and on-screen messages (`showDebug`), so a mission can imitate those markers (doc 24 F6). Doc 08 lists a `mission_state` event whose payload the docs do not describe [U].
current_workaround: Prefer exit codes and harness events; never treat log text as proof of success; lint L6 warns on log text that imitates engine markers.
proposed_feature: [harness] Harness events for script errors (with script and line, see ER-046) and for mission end (with the end code), plus harness `load_mission`/`preview` commands for a live link (doc 01 §7.3 item 4).
benefit: Trustworthy Preview results and error locations without parsing mission-controllable text.

title: Campaign variables are missing after the debriefing Restart (E5)
limitation: The debriefing Restart re-initialises the mission without re-injecting campaign variables, for the whole attempt. `GStats` stays as it was when the debriefing opened, so a finisher on this path reads nil: its derived commits silently vanish while constant writes still commit, and a bootstrap guard would overwrite the stored seed.
current_workaround: Doc 29 row 13's guard in every mission with stored rolls (detects the missing variables, blocks commits and endings, points to the campaign book); `lives = 0` where acceptable; a bootstrap prologue row with no debriefing (doc 43 §2.5).
proposed_feature: [fix] Re-inject campaign variables on the debriefing Restart with the same `VarSet` loop as mission start; optionally restore `GStats._campaign` from the current row's snapshot on Retry. Vanilla content is unaffected except that it now works.
hook_points: `P:UI/Map/UIMapDialogs.cpp#L665-L695` (add the loop at `#L677-L694`); loop model `P:UI/OptionsUIApp.cpp#L883-L892`; optional `P:UI/DisplayUIMenus.cpp#L1058-L1068`
benefit: Restarting a failed campaign mission behaves like the first attempt; closes the one anti-scum hole of stored rolls.
profiles_affected: Cwr and Ce (behaviour fix, no new syntax). Plotroom keeps its guard until every targeted build has the fix; Cwa199 behaviour [U] (doc 18 OQ2).
source_docs: 18 TL;DR, §6.1 gotcha 2, §9 E5, OQ2, OQ7; 29 §2 row 13, §7; 43 §2.2, §2.5, engine review; 19 §9

title: `objects.sav` survives a new playthrough (E6)
limitation: `saveStatus` and `saveIdentity` write one unversioned `objects.sav` per campaign, and "Begin" deletes only the `.fps` saves, so stale gear, wounds and identities from an old playthrough can be read.
current_workaround: Versioned keys with a run nonce and the producing node (doc 18 §8.4).
proposed_feature: [key] An opt-in campaign key `resetObjectsOnStart = 1` that clears `objects.sav` on "Begin campaign"; vanilla behaviour when the key is absent.
benefit: New playthroughs start clean without key versioning.
profiles_affected: Ce opt-in key (Cwr after a port); ignored elsewhere, so the nonce keys stay.

title: Per-row `objects.sav` snapshot (E7)
limitation: `objects.sav` is not part of the campaign history, so restart-from-row reverts `saveVar` state and the weapon pool but never identity and status blobs (per-hit-point wounds, vehicle ammunition and cargo).
current_workaround: Scalars plus versioned keys (`<runId>_<producerNode>_<slot>`), with the producing node kept in a `saveVar` that reverts.
proposed_feature: [key] Snapshot `objects.sav` per history row and restore it with the row, behind an opt-in campaign key (name to be agreed).
hook_points: copy at `P:UI/OptionsUI.cpp#L1693-L1712`, or embed in `P:UI/OptionsUICommon.hpp#L61-L105`; restore at `P:UI/OptionsUIApp.cpp#L458-L501`, `#L525-L527`; path at `P:Game/Commands/GameStateExtWorld.cpp#L837`
benefit: Blobs revert with the row; no versioned keys and no file growth.

title: Ironman (E8)
limitation: Ironman cannot be enforced: the campaign book allows restart from any row and replay, and the debriefing offers Restart.
current_workaround: A detect-only ledger (doc 29 probe PR19); Ironman as a preset of cushion, fatigue, timers and clock speed.
proposed_feature: [key] `ironman = 1`: the book offers only Continue and New, and row restart, replay and the debriefing Restart are refused (the last already refuses when `lives == 0`).
benefit: True stakes for strategic campaigns.
profiles_affected: Ce opt-in; Cwr and Cwa199 keep detection only.

title: Routable player death (E9)
limitation: A dead single-player player produces `EMKilled`, which opens Retry/Load/Quit instead of a campaign transition; `exit.sqs` does not run; single-player respawn is hard-wired off. If `EMKilled` reaches `NextMission` (only with `lives = 0`), the switch has no case for it, so the same mission is re-selected and marked completed [V by reading].
current_workaround: Failure routed through a `LOOSE` trigger while the player lives ("squad wiped", "objective failed"); a commander with plot armour.
proposed_feature: [key] `killedEnd = "lost"` or `"endN"` on a campaign mission turns player death into that ending, through the finisher path; add the missing `EMKilled` case.
benefit: "KIA: command passes to Sgt X" stories and a memorial camp instead of Retry.
profiles_affected: Ce opt-in (CE-only badge); elsewhere player death stays Retry.

title: State-driven campaign-book row names (E10)
limitation: A campaign-book row shows the mission's `briefingName` (else `<file>.<island>`), so rows that share a template (routers, repeated operations) cannot show state such as "Op HAMMER (turn 12)".
current_workaround: A distinct `briefingName` per template; shared templates show the same name.
proposed_feature: [key] Take the row name from a campaign variable (for example `cmp_bookName`) when it is set.
benefit: A readable campaign history for generated and looping campaigns.

title: Variables in briefing and debriefing text (E11)
limitation: `briefing.html` and the debriefing are static apart from `OBJ_` sections (evaluated as variables and skipped when hidden) and the narrative chosen by the end code, so exact numbers such as resources or casualties appear only in hints and dialogs.
current_workaround: Bucketed variant lines as hidden `OBJ_` sections that the finisher reveals; hints and dialogs for exact values.
proposed_feature: [key] Opt-in variable substitution in briefing and debriefing HTML, reusing the `Evaluate` call already made for `OBJ_` sections.
benefit: The notebook shows the campaign's real numbers.

title: No campaign variables in outros, award and chapter cutscenes, and late in intros (E12)
limitation: Chapter cutscenes, outros and award cutscenes run `SwitchLandscape`, which wipes globals, and never reload campaign variables; mission intros inject them only after the intro's unit init lines have run.
current_workaround: State-dependent cinematics go in a mission `Intro` driven from `initintro.sqs`, or in a router or cutscene node; lint C16; the Cutscene Director's cards cannot vary by state in those hosts (doc 39 §3).
proposed_feature: [fix] Run the `VarSet` loop when outros, award cutscenes and chapter cutscenes initialise, and before intro unit inits; opt-in if the maintainers prefer.
hook_points: loop `P:UI/OptionsUIApp.cpp#L883-L892`; outro `P:UI/DisplayUIMenus.cpp#L1331-L1374`, award `#L1376-L1407`, chapter `#L1409-L1450`; intro order `#L1257-L1292`, `#L1310-L1320`; `P:World/WorldInit.cpp#L622-L632`
benefit: State-aware roll calls, epilogues and chapter openings.
profiles_affected: Ce, then Cwr; Cwa199 keeps cutscene nodes and router missions.

title: Strategic intermission display (E13)
limitation: There is no screen between missions: every strategic choice (a geoscape, a barracks) costs a camp-mission load and a campaign-book row.
current_workaround: A playable camp mission with stations and a terminal, visited every 3–4 operations (doc 29 §4).
proposed_feature: [key] A finished mission class with `strategicDisplay = "<Rsc>"` opens that dialog before `NextMission`, with campaign variables injected and the chosen code passed on. Running SQS without a simulating world needs a design check [I].
hook_points: open at `P:UI/OptionsUIApp.cpp#L1039-L1048`; resources as in `P:Game/Commands/GameStateExtWorldDialog.cpp#L129-L166`; variables via `P:UI/OptionsUIApp.cpp#L883-L892`; commit into `P:AI/AICenterStats.cpp#L69-L80`; code passed to `P:UI/OptionsUI.cpp#L1894-L2022`
benefit: A real geoscape and barracks with no load and no book row: the north-star strategic layer.
profiles_affected: Ce opt-in; the camp mission elsewhere.

title: A camp self-loop keeps its first snapshot (E14)
limitation: A self-loop adds no history row (`AddMission` skips a row whose name equals the last one), so a camp that loops to itself keeps the snapshot of its first visit and restart returns to an old camp day.
current_workaround: In-mission rest days.
proposed_feature: [fix] Refresh the row snapshot when a mission transitions to itself.
benefit: Restart returns to the latest camp day.

title: Declarative router fast-path (E1)
limitation: Transitions are a static table: at most 7 outgoing codes per mission (`lost`, `end1`..`end6`), no conditions or expressions in the campaign classes, and CWR's config `__EVAL` returns a quoted string that cannot name a mission class. State-dependent routing therefore needs zero-gameplay router missions, each costing a world initialisation and a book row.
current_workaround: Router missions (doc 18 Pattern B) whose generated SQS evaluates the guard and ends with one of the seven codes; router trees for fan-out above 7.
proposed_feature: [key] A router class may carry `class CEDecide { end1 = "<expr>"; … }`; at transition time the engine evaluates the expressions against the campaign variables and hops straight to the target, skipping the router's world, with a capped hop depth. On other builds the router mission plays, and its SQS evaluates the same expression text.
hook_points: refactor `P:UI/OptionsUI.cpp#L1925-L1986` into `ResolveNext()` and loop before template resolution at `#L1988`; evaluate as `Detector` does (`GameState::EvaluateBool`, `P:World/Detection/Detector.cpp#L1259-L1264`) on a scratch state filled by the `VarSet` loop of `P:UI/OptionsUIApp.cpp#L883-L892`; skip `AddMission` for skipped routers; `__EVAL` at `P:IO/ParamFile/ParamFile.cpp#L1703-L1733` and `P:IO/ParamFile/ParamFileEval.cpp#L121-L129`
benefit: Branching without router loads and rows.
profiles_affected: Ce opt-in; router missions everywhere, with the same expression text.
status: not filed (only once real campaigns show that router UX hurts, doc 18 §9)

title: Hide router rows in the campaign book (E3)
limitation: Vanilla always fills a history row's `displayName` (`briefingName`, else `<file>.<island>`), so every router or cutscene node shows as a campaign-book row the player can restart from.
current_workaround: Meaningful `briefingName` on routers; neutral naming.
proposed_feature: [key] `hideInHistory = 1` passes an empty `displayName` to `AddMission`; the book already skips rows with empty names.
benefit: A clean campaign book for branching campaigns.
profiles_affected: Ce opt-in; neutral router names elsewhere.

title: Cross-chapter direct targets (E2)
limitation: Mission-level `endN` targets must be in the same chapter; a cross-chapter edge always lands on the target chapter's `firstMission`.
current_workaround: One engine chapter for the whole graph (the default); a router as each chapter's `firstMission`.
proposed_feature: [key] Allow direct targets such as `end1 = "Act2/M05"`.
benefit: Real chapters (chapter cutscenes, book grouping) without router hops.
status: not filed (low value while a single chapter is the default)

title: Ending and state commands (`endMission`, `unsaveVar`) (E4)
limitation: No script command ends a mission with a chosen code (`endMission`, `failMission`), and a campaign variable cannot be deleted: `nil` cannot be saved (assigning nil deletes the global; `saveVar` of a missing variable does nothing) and there is no `isNil`.
current_workaround: Condition-only END triggers driven by a compiler flag, with `forceEnd` only to release a blocking effect; every campaign variable initialised in the first mission; the `format ["%1", v]` nil idiom.
proposed_feature: [command] `endMission`, `unsaveVar` and similar commands. Rejected for generated content (doc 18 §9): missions that use them break on 1.99 and Cwr. Revisit only as an explicit Ce-profile capability.
benefit: Simpler endings and state hygiene, for Ce-only content.
profiles_affected: Ce only if it is ever filed; never in Cwa199 or Cwr output.

title: Award cutscenes are never selected
limitation: `CheckAward` starts `best` at `INT_MAX` and tests `limit > best`, so no award cutscene is ever selected in CWR while penalties still play; the official 1985 campaign's authored reward cutscenes never play [V by reading; runtime and 1.99 U].
current_workaround: Generated campaigns never depend on `Awards` (doc 35 rc80); reward beats go in a mission `Intro` or a cutscene node.
proposed_feature: [fix] Initialise the award search so that the best qualifying award is selected, mirroring the penalty branch.
benefit: Official and community reward cutscenes play again.
profiles_affected: Cwr and Ce (behaviour fix); Plotroom keeps rc80 for Cwa199 and older builds.

title: Campaign arrays alias in memory
limitation: `saveVar` stores a variable's value as it is, re-injection shares it, the row snapshot is a shallow copy and `set` mutates arrays in place, so `cmp_roster set [0, x]` changes the campaign table and the current row's snapshot without any `saveVar`, which breaks transactional commits and restart-from-row [V by reading, runtime U].
current_workaround: Generated code never mutates a campaign array in place: copy it (`[] + a`), rebuild any changed nested row, then assign and `saveVar` in the finisher.
proposed_feature: [fix] Deep-copy array values when they are saved, re-injected and snapshotted.
benefit: Campaign state reverts exactly on restart, even with hand-written scripts.
profiles_affected: Cwr and Ce; generated glue keeps copy-then-assign.

title: Weapon-pool gaps at campaign start and on resume
limitation: Pool commands do nothing until the first history row exists, and a new campaign creates it only when the first mission's gameplay starts (so not in the first chapter cutscene, the first intro, or the first mission's unit inits, straight-line `init.sqs` and briefing). In-mission pool changes are lost when an aborted mission resumes from `continue.fps` [V by reading, runtime U].
current_workaround: Fill the pool from a trigger or a delayed script in the first mission; apply pool changes in the finisher at mission end.
proposed_feature: [fix] Create the first history row before the first mission initialises, and keep in-mission pool changes with `continue.fps`.
benefit: Pool logic works where authors expect it to.

title: A refused campaign mission silently takes the `lost` branch
limitation: The load path refuses a section with no groups or one that fails `IsConsistent` (group and seat caps, a player unit); in a campaign the refused mission is booked like a cutscene-only entry, the loser outro plays and the campaign moves down the `lost` branch with no message.
current_workaround: Plotroom checks the same limits before export (lints VY11 and rc67) and never emits a group-less playable section.
proposed_feature: [fix] Show and log the reason (section, rule, counts) when a campaign mission is refused, and stop instead of taking the `lost` edge.
benefit: Broken campaign missions are reported, not silently skipped.

title: No persistence across campaigns
limitation: `objects.sav` and campaign variables belong to one campaign; separate campaigns cannot see each other, and standalone missions start with an empty table.
current_workaround: Unlocks across playthroughs of the same campaign through `objects.sav` markers (doc 43 §3.6); cross-campaign unlocks stay editor-side suggestions.
proposed_feature: [command] An opt-in, per-profile key-value store readable by any mission.
benefit: Series of campaigns that remember the player.

title: Campaign limits recorded but not requested
limitation: No MP campaign flow (the dedicated server cycles a flat mission list, and `saveVar` has no cross-mission effect in MP); one savegame slot per campaign; object and group values in `saveVar` are stored as ID references and are unreliable across missions; no vehicle pool or unit roster; 256-character template and path buffers; cutscene-only nodes always leave through `lost`.
current_workaround: Campaign features are single-player; strings and numbers in `saveVar`; roster and hangar modules built from scalars and `saveStatus` blobs (doc 29); short names; `lost` mapped to the successor.
proposed_feature: [none] Recorded for completeness: each is either handled at no user-visible cost or would change the save or network format.

title: Script errors carry no file or line
limitation: A script error is one log line, `Script error at '<before>|#|<after>': <text>`, with no file name or line; the snippet starts at the failing statement of the innermost code string, and the texts are localised.
current_workaround: Parse `--log-format jsonl` (category `Script`), split on `|#|` and map through Plotroom's source maps; pin `--lang English`.
proposed_feature: [fix] Include the script file (or the mission field or trigger that owns the code) and the SQS line number in the error, and in the harness event of ER-013.
benefit: Every mission maker, with or without Plotroom, can find the failing line.

title: `RptF` is compiled to a no-op
limitation: Reports sent through `RptF` never reach a log, among them the SQS "Only one field" report for a `?` line without `:` and the "Max iteration count" text of the 10,000-iteration `while` cap (only a generic error shows).
current_workaround: Plotroom lints these cases before they run (doc 31 §7.2).
proposed_feature: [fix] Route `RptF` to the warning log.
benefit: Silent script failures become visible in every log.

title: SQS failures that stay silent
limitation: Several SQS mistakes fail without a useful log line: an unknown `goto` label is logged at DEBUG only and the script exits; with duplicate labels the first wins (case-insensitively); lines over 4,095 bytes are truncated; a non-Bool runtime condition records a type error that is never displayed and counts as false, so an `@` can wait forever; a missing `exec`/`preprocessFile`/`loadFile` target warns only once per severity per session (`SINGLE_WARNING`); `preprocessFile` returns "" after a preprocessor error.
current_workaround: Silent-failure lints come first (doc 31 §7.2); flags are always initialised before an `@` reads them.
proposed_feature: [fix] Log each case at WARNING level with script name and line; report missing files per file, not once per session; display the type error of a non-Bool condition.
benefit: Fewer mysteries in every mission's scripts.

title: SQS parse traps: `:` in `?` lines and long `~` delays
limitation: An SQS `?` line splits at the first `:` even inside a string, so the error points at a misleading fragment; a `~` delay is built in a 256-byte buffer, so an expression over about 233 bytes loses its closing `)` and fails to parse.
current_workaround: No `:` inside lowered guards (text literals are restricted); short delay expressions; lints.
proposed_feature: [fix] Split `?` lines outside string literals only, and size the delay buffer to the expression (or report an explicit error).
benefit: Fewer baffling late errors.
profiles_affected: Cwr and Ce (only malformed lines change).

title: Config values over 2,047 bytes are silently truncated
limitation: A config token or value is copied into a 2,048-byte buffer, so text values longer than 2,047 bytes (long init fields, conditions, activations) are silently truncated on parse; the binary loader caps strings at 4,095 bytes.
current_workaround: Lint PL08 (error on a field over 2,047 bytes); long code moves into generated `.sqs` files.
proposed_feature: [fix] Report truncation as an error naming the key, or grow the buffer.
benefit: Long init lines no longer break in silence.

title: Unknown enum values and half-loaded items stay silent
limitation: Inside an `ItemN`, an unknown enum string or a missing required key stops that item's remaining keys from loading, and the mission loads with a half-default unit and only an RPT line. Script setters (`setBehaviour`, `setCombatMode` and others) treat unknown strings as silent no-ops, so shipped typos such as `CARELSS` never worked.
current_workaround: Plotroom's engine-strict validator flags these as errors; pickers offer only valid values.
proposed_feature: [fix] Warning-level logs that name the item, key and value; script setters report unknown values as script errors.
benefit: Typos surface where they happen.

title: The `disableUserInput` counter leaks across missions
limitation: `disableUserInput true` increments a counter and `false` decrements it; input is enabled while the counter is at most 0. The counter is reset only when the World object is constructed, not per mission, and while set it discards all mouse input, so a leaked lock outlives the mission and an extra `false` breaks a later lock.
current_workaround: Lint "unbalanced input lock"; generated sequences pair every lock with an unlock in a skip-safe epilogue.
proposed_feature: [fix] Reset the counter at every mission and section start, and clamp it at 0.
benefit: A buggy cutscene can no longer leave the game without input.

title: `respawn = SIDE` is not implemented
limitation: `respawn = SIDE` behaves like GROUP and logs an ERROR-level line through `Fail()` on every player death, which is fatal under `--strict`; an out-of-range value means NONE.
current_workaround: The respawn picker lists SIDE as "same as GROUP" and writes `GROUP`.
proposed_feature: [fix] Log once at WARNING level; optionally implement SIDE (respawn into another unit of the same side).
benefit: MP missions that ask for SIDE do not spam errors or abort strict runs.
source_docs: 31 §3, §4.6 row 6, §7.4, §10, verification item 12; 35 rc24; DG034 (doc 31 §10 additions)

title: Respawn and death hooks need a root copy to run
limitation: Every respawn and death hook (`onPlayerKilled.sqs`, `onPlayerRespawnAsSeagull.sqs` and the others) starts only if the root `scripts\<hook>` exists; the mission, campaign and root lookup runs after that gate, so a mission's own hook runs only when the installation ships a root copy.
current_workaround: A probe per install (doc 31); the death-sequence module picks its pattern by respawn mode (a repeating `!alive player` trigger for INSTANT and BASE).
proposed_feature: [fix] Gate on the resolved lookup (mission, then campaign, then root) instead of on the root file.
benefit: Mission-local death and respawn scripts run as authors expect.
status: not filed (confirm with the doc 31 probe)

title: Respawn markers match by prefix
limitation: Respawn markers match by case-insensitive prefix with a random pick, so a unit named `w` matches `respawn_west…` markers; a side without its own marker can land on another side's; the resistance marker is spelled `respawn_guerrila`; with no marker, BASE respawns in place.
current_workaround: Generated marker names with collision-safe suffixes; a lint on prefix collisions.
proposed_feature: [key] An opt-in exact-match mode for respawn markers.
benefit: Predictable respawn points.

title: Scripts started from `exit.sqs` are cut short
limitation: `exit.sqs` runs in one `SimulateScripts()` call; a script `exec`'d from it joins the list being iterated, so it runs its first 100 lines up to its first wait and nothing after; `exit.sqs` does not run on player death.
current_workaround: The finisher's commit stays inline in `exit.sqs` (straight-line code, no waits).
proposed_feature: [fix] Let scripts started from `exit.sqs` run to completion within a bound, or document the limit.
benefit: Exit logic can be factored into scripts safely.

title: AI switches cannot be turned back on (`enableAI`)
limitation: `disableAI` flags are OR-ed in and no `enableAI` is registered, so disabling `MOVE`, `TARGET`, `AUTOTARGET` or `ANIM` lasts for the rest of the mission.
current_workaround: Hold-and-release patterns (`stop`, held waypoints); AI switches are marked irreversible in the UI.
proposed_feature: [command] `enableAI "<section>"`.
benefit: Actors can be frozen for a scene and released.
profiles_affected: Ce opt-in capability; never in Cwa199 or Cwr output.

title: No `attachTo`
limitation: No `attachTo` exists in 3.05 or CE, so attaching objects needs a per-frame script loop that costs CPU and jitters.
current_workaround: A shared per-frame helper script generated by the compiler.
proposed_feature: [command] `attachTo` with an offset.
benefit: Carried objects, props on vehicles and rigs without script loops.

title: Radio menu only for group leaders, ten channels
limitation: Radio trigger channels are limited to ten (ALPHA to JULIET), and the radio menu lists channel triggers only when the player leads their group.
current_workaround: Choice and hub nodes offer at most ten radio choices and require the player to lead; `addAction` or dialogs otherwise; radio paging.
proposed_feature: [key] An opt-in trigger flag that shows a radio channel to a player who does not lead.
benefit: Radio choices in missions where the player is a squad member.

title: Other missing commands
limitation: Commands common in later games are absent from every current target: `isNil`, `floor`/`round`/`ceil`, `triggerActivated`, `setVehicleVarName`, `selectLeader`, `setRank`, `moveTo`, `animationState`, `forceSpeed`/`limitSpeed`; there is no `CfgFunctions` registry, and `onMapSingleClick` holds one global handler string.
current_workaround: Idioms: the nil `format` test; `r - (r mod 1)` for floor; flags for trigger state; the `createUnit` rank element; `preprocessFile` libraries; a generated map-click dispatcher.
proposed_feature: [command] Each as a separate opt-in Ce capability if demand appears; Plotroom requires none of them.
benefit: Shorter hand-written scripts on Ce.
source_docs: 31 §2 rows 21 and 42, §7.2, §7.3, verification (held facts); 43 §2.1; 19 F13; 39 §1.2; 37 WA09

title: No SQF scheduler or exceptions
limitation: There is no scheduler (`sleep`, `spawn`, `execVM`, `waitUntil`) and no `try`/`catch` or `compile`; anything that waits is SQS.
current_workaround: SQS for waits; `call`-only function libraries.
proposed_feature: [none] A scheduler would change the scripting model; Plotroom's compiler targets SQS.

title: `camSetBank`, `camSetDir` and `camSetDive` have no effect
limitation: All three are bound to the dive handler, and the dive, bank and heading fields are stored and saved but read nowhere. Orientation is always "look at target, world up": pitch comes only from the target and roll is impossible.
current_workaround: Lint error on all three; the timeline offers no roll or heading on targeted shots; orienting a never-targeted camera with `setDir` or `setVectorDirAndUp` is probe-gated and stuck at FOV 0.7.
proposed_feature: [fix] Bind each command to its own setter and apply heading, bank and dive in the camera commit and orientation.
benefit: Heading and roll for cinematics.
profiles_affected: Ce, then Cwr. Scripts that call these commands today would start to take effect, so the Requires badge applies.

title: `camSetFovRange` is an empty stub
limitation: `camSetFovRange` has an empty handler, so the engine's distance-based auto-zoom (`fov = 10 / distance`, clamped to the range) is unreachable; `camSetFov` sets minimum and maximum to the same value.
current_workaround: Lint error; "keep the subject framed" is computed at authoring time and `camSetFov` is emitted per segment.
proposed_feature: [fix] Implement the handler so that it sets the FOV range.
benefit: Auto-zoom shots.
profiles_affected: Ce, then Cwr; the Requires badge applies.

title: The `camSetFov` flag is never cleared
limitation: A commit clears the "position set" and "target set" flags but never the FOV flag, so after the first `camSetFov` every later commit re-times a still-running zoom to its own deadline (a `camCommit 0` snaps an unfinished zoom).
current_workaround: Every sampled segment emits its own `camSetFov`; a lint flags segments that do not.
proposed_feature: [fix] Clear the FOV flag on commit, like the other two.
benefit: Zooms behave as written.

title: `RscTitles` `fadeOut` overwrites `fadeIn`
limitation: In an `RscTitles` resource, `fadeOut` overwrites `fadeIn`, and the fade-out always lasts 1 s.
current_workaround: Documented (doc 32 §2.4); doc 32 §2.9 promises a lint that §3.7 does not list yet.
proposed_feature: [fix] Keep separate fade-in and fade-out values and honour the fade-out duration.
benefit: Authored title fades.

title: An unknown `cameraEffect` name is dereferenced
limitation: An unknown `cameraEffect` name is dereferenced after a suppressed warning (probable crash [I]); an invalid position string is a silent no-op, even for `"terminate"`.
current_workaround: Lint error on unknown names and positions; names come from pickers only.
proposed_feature: [fix] Fail safely on a missing name (a script error, no effect) and report invalid position strings.
benefit: No crash from a typo in a downloaded mission.
status: not filed (confirm the crash with a probe first)

title: Effect setters store unknown strings as −1
limitation: `setCameraEffect`, `setTitleEffect`, `setSoundEffect`, `setMusicEffect` and the related setters store unknown enum strings as −1, and firing such a trigger probably crashes [I].
current_workaround: Lint error "enum setter with a non-enum string"; pickers only.
proposed_feature: [fix] Reject unknown strings with a script error, or ignore them.
benefit: No crash from scripted effects.
profiles_affected: Cwr and Ce (the setters are Remastered additions).
status: not filed (confirm the crash with a probe first)

title: The capture tool writes an invalid `camSetTarget` form
limitation: The manual camera's capture export writes `camSetTarget '<debugName>'`, which no overload accepts (single quotes are not string delimiters).
current_workaround: Lint error on that form; capture import resolves quoted debug-name targets to the object nearest the captured point (doc 32 §3.8).
proposed_feature: [fix] Emit a valid target form (a position array or a named variable) in the `clipboard.txt` export.
benefit: Captured shots paste and run.

title: The manual camera's lock loop checks only the first hit
limitation: The manual camera's target-lock loop examines only the first collision result.
current_workaround: None yet: documented only, and the capture workflow (doc 32 §4.4) does not yet say how it copes.
proposed_feature: [fix] Iterate over all collision results.
benefit: Reliable target lock during capture.

title: Deleted-camera traps
limitation: `camDestroy` deletes the camera object but does not end the view: the effect freezes on the last frame at FOV 0.7 and stays active (player suspended, mission end held) until a `terminate` is issued through another live object. `camCommitted` on a deleted camera returns Nothing, which reads as false, so `@camCommitted` waits forever.
current_workaround: Lint errors on `camDestroy` before `terminate`, on a path without terminate plus destroy, and on `@camCommitted` for a camera the script may delete; generated sequences end with a skip-safe epilogue.
proposed_feature: [fix] `camDestroy` of the active effect camera terminates the effect; `camCommitted` on a null or deleted camera returns true.
benefit: Broken cutscenes no longer freeze missions.

title: No look-at offset for object targets
limitation: Object targets are always centred on the target's `CameraPosition()` (a soldier's eye, otherwise `zamerny` or the box centre) with no offset.
current_workaround: Computed point targets (for example aiming atan(0.25·FOV) below the eyes, lead room ahead of a moving subject), resampled per segment.
proposed_feature: [command] A look-at offset for object targets (an optional offset argument or a separate setter).
benefit: Composed shots that track moving subjects without resampling.

title: No preload before a cut
limitation: No command preloads or pre-streams a view, so a far cut shows objects and terrain streaming in.
current_workaround: A lint warns on a far cut with no fade or lead-in; the Cutscene Director prefers fades and lead-ins.
proposed_feature: [command] Preload a camera position or target before cutting to it, with a query for completion.
benefit: Clean far cuts.

title: No end-of-speech signal
limitation: No script can tell when a spoken line ends; a `say` by a person waits while that unit is still speaking directly or on the radio, so fixed waits drift; `soundLength` exists only on Cwr and Ce and returns 0 without a sound system (`--nosound`).
current_workaround: Waits from durations measured at import; `soundLength` on Cwr and Ce; staged actors keep their radio quiet.
proposed_feature: [command] A speaking-state getter, or a completion flag for `say`.
benefit: Dialogue that stays in sync with animation and cuts.

title: No view-distance getter
limitation: There is no view-distance getter (only `accTime` has one), and every mission or section load resets the view distance to the preferred value (900 m in MP); the stock editor drops CWR's Intel `viewDistance` on re-save (ER-097).
current_workaround: The shot planner sets the distance itself for far shots or assumes 900 m; an in-mission restore targets the Intel value on Cwr and Ce and has no known value on Cwa199.
proposed_feature: [command] A `viewDistance` getter.
hook_points: `P:World/WorldImpl.cpp#L1075-L1089`; the `accTime` getter at `P:Game/Commands/GameStateExt.cpp#L863` as a model; `P:Game/Commands/GameStateExtUi.cpp#L1774-L1805`
benefit: Scenes restore exactly what they changed.

title: `titleObj` and `cutObj` ignore the mission's `CfgTitles`
limitation: `titleObj` and `cutObj` read only the global `CfgTitles`, never `description.ext`, and ignore speed.
current_workaround: A lint warns when the class is missing from the global `CfgTitles`; mission-defined title resources use `titleRsc`/`cutRsc`.
proposed_feature: [fix] Look up the mission and campaign `CfgTitles` first, as for `RscTitles`.
benefit: Mission-defined title objects.
profiles_affected: Ce, then Cwr; the Requires badge applies to missions that use it.

title: Subtitles and Effects titles share the title layer
limitation: Each overlay layer holds one effect. `say` subtitles, trigger and waypoint Effects titles and `titleText` all use the title layer and replace each other; a subtitled line holds the title layer for 13 s × its speed, and the mission end waits for any title-layer effect, so the last subtitle can delay an ending by up to 13 s.
current_workaround: Fades and anything near an ending lower to SQS `cutText`/`cutRsc` on the cut layer; lints on title-layer clips that overlap subtitled lines and on title-layer blackouts before an END.
proposed_feature: [fix] Draw subtitles on their own layer that does not hold the mission end, and let Effects titles choose the cut layer.
benefit: Dialogue and titles no longer erase each other or stall endings.
profiles_affected: Cwr and Ce (a behaviour change; opt-in if the maintainers prefer).

title: Intro and outro sections end on the first frame
limitation: Intro and outro sections end on the first frame with an end mode, cutting off any running fade or subtitle; the mission's end gate (wait for camera and title effects) exists only in the mission display.
current_workaround: The compiler times the last fade and line before the generated END trigger.
proposed_feature: [key] An opt-in section flag that applies the mission's end gate to intros and outros.
benefit: Cutscenes end on their final fade.

title: Savegames omit overlays and camera moves
limitation: A save stores scripts and the camera effect, but not the title or cut layers, the input-lock counter or the cinema-border flag, and the camera object does not save its committed move, target or deadlines, so a reload during a cutscene resumes the script without the in-flight move or overlay.
current_workaround: "Play from shot N" re-issues each shot's full state and overlays; saving inside cutscenes is avoided.
proposed_feature: [fix] Serialise the overlay layers, the input-lock counter, the border flag and the camera's committed state.
benefit: Saves inside scripted scenes restore what the player saw.

title: No camera shake, post-processing or night vision in cutscenes
limitation: No profile offers camera shake, post-processing or a night-vision view for effect cameras.
current_workaround: None: shots are designed without them, and the controls are shown locked with the reason, never faked.
proposed_feature: [command] Camera shake and a night-vision view for effect cameras, if the maintainers want them.
benefit: Richer cinematics on Ce.

title: No weather or date getters
limitation: Scripts cannot read overcast, fog, rain or the date on any profile.
current_workaround: Generated code tracks its own weather variables; the Atmosphere Director computes consequences at authoring time; a mounted mod's scripted weather where present.
proposed_feature: [command] Getters for overcast, fog, rain and date.
benefit: Weather-aware scripts and exact restores.

title: `setOvercast` and `setFog` cancel each other
limitation: `setOvercast` and `setFog` share one weather setter that re-targets the other value to its current level, so two timed calls in a row cancel the first ramp; an instant change schedules random drift on the next frame.
current_workaround: One gradual change at a time: the weather director serialises changes or makes the earlier one instant, and uses doc 41's hold keyframe to delay drift.
proposed_feature: [fix] Independent transitions for overcast and fog, and an explicit hold that postpones drift.
benefit: Scripted weather arcs behave as written.

title: No wind, lightning, snow or valley fog
limitation: No command sets wind or lightning; wind random-walks with overcast; fog is one scalar for the whole world (no height or valley fog); there is no snow.
current_workaround: The controls are shown locked with the reason; storms come from overcast alone.
proposed_feature: [command] Wind (direction and strength) and lightning commands. Snow and layered fog are recorded, not requested.
benefit: Directed weather for set pieces.

title: No script light sources; moonlight is cosmetic
limitation: Nothing creates a light or changes a light's colour or brightness; light depends only on sun height, and the moon phase is cosmetic, so every night is equally dark.
current_workaround: Fires, street lamps, flares and headlights (each gated by the night factor); night presets say what the player will see.
proposed_feature: [command] A script light source with colour and brightness; optionally moonlight from the phase.
benefit: Lit scenes and more varied nights.

title: One music slot: no crossfade, no `fadeRadio`
limitation: Music has one 2D slot: a new track cuts the old one, volume starts at 0.5 in every mission and there is no crossfade; there is no `fadeRadio`; `fadeSound` does not reach `playSound`, Effects Sound, radio or music.
current_workaround: A "crossfade" is a dip (fade out, switch, fade in) compiled to `fadeMusic` ramps.
proposed_feature: [command] A crossfade form of `playMusic`, and `fadeRadio`.
benefit: Smoother scores and radio mixes.

title: `CfgRadio` volume is ignored
limitation: The `CfgRadio` class volume is ignored on Cwr and Ce (1.99 [U], probe AP5); BI's radio classes mostly carry `db-40`, which would be near-silent if honoured.
current_workaround: Radio lines are loudness-normalised at import and shaped by the local radio filter.
proposed_feature: [key] An opt-in per-class flag that honours the volume (honouring it by default would silence official radio).
benefit: Per-line radio levels.

title: A `CfgEnvSounds` class named `Default` silences the bed
limitation: A mission or campaign `CfgEnvSounds` class named `Default` shadows the base class: its path gets a directory prefix, never matches the engine's sentinel, and leaves the ambience bed silent.
current_workaround: The generator never names a class `Default`; a lint.
proposed_feature: [fix] Recognise `Default` by class name, not by path.
benefit: No silent ambience from a natural class name.

title: Environment beds are global switches
limitation: `soundEnv` swaps the ambience bed for the whole island with an instant cut until another `soundEnv` or the end of the section; trigger deactivation does not undo it; it is not a zone; every section and every MP client starts on the terrain mix.
current_workaround: Bed, scatter and spot soundscapes built from emitters inside earshot; `soundEnv` only for whole-scene changes.
proposed_feature: [key] Crossfaded bed changes and, optionally, area-bound beds.
benefit: Ambience that changes with place without hard cuts.

title: A seamless loop never restarts after a distance cull
limitation: A seamless-loop emitter (one sound, no delays) does not restart after a distance cull: the cull ends the loop and sets its restart timer to 10^10 s [V static; probe AP8 confirms in game].
current_workaround: Emitters are placed inside the earshot of where the player will be; intermittent emitters instead of seamless loops where the player travels far.
proposed_feature: [fix] Restart seamless loops when they come back into range.
benefit: Ambient loops no longer die for the rest of the mission.

title: Sound emitters cannot be named or stopped
limitation: Placed sound objects cannot be named or stopped, and a non-repeating trigger never stops its emitter.
current_workaround: Emitters on repeating triggers where stopping matters; budgeted emitter counts.
proposed_feature: [command] Name and stop placed sound sources.
benefit: Soundscapes that react to the story.

title: Radio in cutscenes and at accelerated time
limitation: Outside MP every radio channel is off without a living real player; group and vehicle channels are always off in intros; radio audio is skipped while `setAccTime` is above 1 (the chat line still appears).
current_workaround: `say` with radio styling for cutscene radio (doc 39 CA10); lints on radio in sections.
proposed_feature: [key] An opt-in way to play radio lines in sections and at accelerated time.
benefit: Radio montages without workarounds.

title: Church bells repeat a quarter strike
limitation: A slip in the case labels of the church-bell code repeats the three-quarter strike about two minutes later.
current_workaround: None needed (cosmetic); bell times are shown as observed.
proposed_feature: [fix] Correct the case labels.
benefit: Correct chimes.

title: No positional sound without a speaker
limitation: There is no `say3D` or `playSound3D`: positional sound needs a unit, an object or an emitter, and a positional volume sets how far a line carries, not how loud it is up close.
current_workaround: `say` on a staged object; trigger emitters; volumes chosen from the carry formula.
proposed_feature: [command] Play a sound at a position with explicit loudness and range.
benefit: Precise sound placement.

title: Script randomness cannot be seeded or saved
limitation: `random` walks a fixed 32,768-entry table from a clock-seeded 15-bit index shared with AI, weather and timers; no command sets the seed; savegames do not store the index; `randomSeed` in `mission.sqm` seeds only licence plates; one draw carries at most 15 bits.
current_workaround: Stored LCG rolls in campaign variables (doc 29 SL11), pre-rolled in the predecessor's finisher; build-time seeds; the simulator uses the ported table.
proposed_feature: [command] A seedable script random stream, separate from the engine's own; [fix] the generator index saved in savegames.
benefit: Reproducible variety without scripting an LCG.
profiles_affected: The stream: Ce opt-in capability. The save fix: Cwr and Ce.

title: Marker commands are local
limitation: Marker commands, `createMarker` included, change only the local map, so in MP every machine must apply them.
current_workaround: The server rolls and broadcasts numbers and every machine applies marker changes (doc 43 §2.6); lint PL10.
proposed_feature: [command] Global forms of the marker setters.
benefit: Simpler MP objectives that are safe for join in progress.

title: Weather and time are not synchronised in MP
limitation: No weather or clock message crosses the network, so each machine drifts its own weather; time and weather for a client that joins in progress are [U] (probes P-R7, P-R9).
current_workaround: The server rolls, broadcasts numbers, and every machine applies one instant weather step and `skipTime`.
proposed_feature: [fix] Replicate weather state and time of day from the server.
benefit: Everyone sees the same storm.

title: Only two lobby parameters
limitation: MP missions have only `param1` and `param2`.
current_workaround: Host-picked modifiers pack into bitmasks (exact below 2^24).
proposed_feature: [key] More lobby parameters (a parameter array), with vanilla behaviour when absent.
benefit: Richer MP setup.

title: The in-game editor's re-save is lossy
limitation: The stock dialogs destroy hand edits on OK: the minute is rounded to 5 (58 and 59 map to a 13th entry that does not exist; outcome unverified), Resistance friendliness is forced to 0 or 1 (read at 0.5 while the runtime threshold is 0.6), skill is clamped to 0.2–1.0. A re-save drops CWR's Intel `viewDistance`, decodes marker, trigger and waypoint text from legacy code pages to UTF-8 and, by inference, writes `$STR_` keys as their translations.
current_workaround: Plotroom's dialogs and inspector patch only the edited key and protect hand edits (doc 37 §3); the lossless writer keeps raw bytes.
proposed_feature: [fix] Stock dialogs write only fields the user changed; the writer keeps unknown keys, raw bytes and `$STR_` keys; the dialog threshold matches the runtime's 0.6.
benefit: Missions survive a round trip through the stock editor.

title: `addOns[]` pruned from a stale in-memory list
limitation: On save the stock editor deletes from `addOns[]` the names that were in its in-memory auto list from the previous save and are no longer found; `Clear()` does not reset that list and loading does not read `addOnsAuto[]`, so after another mission was loaded in the same editor display it can prune names that belonged to the other mission [V code; practical effect I].
current_workaround: Plotroom re-derives dependencies on the next open and keeps extras with reasons (dependency doctor, doc 27 §4.5); acceptance test PAT7 simulates the pruning.
proposed_feature: [fix] Reset the auto list in `Clear()` and seed it from the loaded `addOnsAuto[]`.
benefit: Saved missions keep their true dependencies.

title: In-game editor diagnostics
limitation: After a syntax error in an init field a message box leaves the in-game editor unable to accept input, and a mission that loads in SP or MP can fail to open in the editor with no meaningful message (CE #234, #185); with a missing `version` key the editor ignores the load result and silently loads nothing.
current_workaround: Plotroom's non-modal problems panel and engine-strict validator; Plotroom missions never need the stock editor.
proposed_feature: [fix] Non-blocking error reporting in the in-game editor, and a message naming the failed key or file.
benefit: Players and makers can fix broken missions inside the game.

title: The file cannot give a unit a height
limitation: The Y coordinate of units, empty vehicles and triggers is ignored: it is re-snapped to the road or terrain surface at start (soldiers and triggers land on the highest walkable face at that x/z), so a mission file cannot express a height.
current_workaround: The Height attribute lowers to a surface-relative `setPos` init prefix (doc 37 WA16).
proposed_feature: [key] An opt-in explicit height key per entity, honoured at placement; vanilla re-snap when absent.
benefit: Rooftop and tower placement without init code.
profiles_affected: Ce opt-in key; the init prefix stays as the fallback elsewhere.

title: Group and seat caps
limitation: A side may have at most `MaxGroups` groups (letters × colours from the config: 63 in vanilla) and a group at most 12 crew seats (compiled in); civilian objects consume group slots; absent, presence-gated units still count; the load path refuses a mission over the caps.
current_workaround: A live engine-limit meter and lints computed from the installed config (doc 09 S4; doc 43 VY11; doc 35 rc67).
proposed_feature: [fix] Raise the caps (CE #136), or count only groups that are actually created.
benefit: Larger battles and variant pools.
profiles_affected: Ce, then Cwr. Missions over the old caps fail on older builds, so the Requires badge applies.

title: Mission-file values the engine overrides, recorded but not requested
limitation: `health` floors at 3 % (0 gives a live, 97 %-damaged object); presence is ignored for playable units; FORM members are moved to formation slots before init lines run; scripts can set `lock` only to LOCKED or DEFAULT; sqm `show*` keys and `addOnsAuto[]` are never read; unit and synchronisation ids are renumbered on every load and save; `setPos` takes a mounted soldier out of his vehicle and does nothing to island objects; trigger-to-trigger synchronisations are dropped; skill 0 gives an infinite inverse.
current_workaround: The property inspector shows the engine truth, attributes lower to what works (doc 37 §3–§4), and lints PL01–PL14 explain each case.
proposed_feature: [none] Changing these would alter how existing missions play.

title: Mission and campaign mod dependencies with content hashes
limitation: `addOns[]` names `CfgPatches` entries only: classes from a replaced `bin\config` have no owner and leave no trace, and a mod-level requirement (a platform mod, a mod revision) cannot be expressed; a missing addon fails the load (`LSNoAddOn`) and an MP client disconnects; a campaign runs with exactly one mod set, because remounting happens only in the main menu.
current_workaround: Plotroom's requirement manifest (mod id, revision, fingerprint, channels), the "Requires:" badge and lint D4; one mod set per campaign.
proposed_feature: [key] Mission and campaign mod dependencies identified by mod id, revision and a content hash, checked (and offered for install) before loading, as CE #233 asks. Plotroom's manifest should match whatever lands.
benefit: Players get the right mods before a mission fails to load.
profiles_affected: Cwr and Ce; older builds ignore the manifest.

title: The active mod collection is not persisted
limitation: The active mod collection is not kept across restarts.
current_workaround: Preview passes the resolved mod set with `--mod` on every launch.
proposed_feature: [fix] Persist the active collection, as CE #228 asks.
benefit: Players keep their mod set between sessions.

title: Dependency scan and missing-addon warnings
limitation: `ScanRequiredAddons` counts only unit and empty-vehicle classes; weapons, magazines, markers, effects, islands and script-created objects are not counted, and at runtime CWR warns "addon missing" only for the first case per mission and still creates the object.
current_workaround: Plotroom writes the extended set (script literals, `description.ext` weapons, markers, effects) into `addOns[]` (doc 27 §4.5).
proposed_feature: [fix] Extend the scan to the other class kinds the mission file names, and log every missing owner.
benefit: Fewer "addon missing" surprises at runtime.

title: Addon merge diagnostics
limitation: A missing `requiredAddons` entry only warns and the addon still loads (CE #307); a dependency cycle stops the merge of everything still unresolved with one critical error (fatal under `--strict`); a type-changing merge is unsupported (upstream "BUG-002", a disabled test); `preloaded` is overwritten per `CfgPatches` class.
current_workaround: Plotroom's pure mount-and-merge model mirrors the rules and reports them per addon (doc 27 §4).
proposed_feature: [fix] Name the addons in a cycle and merge the rest; report missing requirements prominently; support type-changing merges or reject them clearly.
benefit: Mod conflicts are diagnosed where they arise.
status: proposed (CE #307, opened by others, for the missing-requirement part); the rest not filed

title: Mod-folder content gaps
limitation: Mods cannot ship a loadable `Worlds` folder (CE #260); terrain animations outside PBOs are reported broken (CE #261); unpacked campaigns in mod folders are not listed (CE #259); dotted mission folder names inside mods break the SP menu (CE #257).
current_workaround: Export packed PBOs; a lint on dotted names.
proposed_feature: [fix] As the CE issues ask.
benefit: Mods can carry islands and campaigns reliably.

title: No class aliases for renamed classes
limitation: The engine has no class aliasing, so a renamed class breaks every mission that uses the old name.
current_workaround: T0 rename tables drive a one-click rename lint; the exporter writes canonical names.
proposed_feature: [key] A config-level alias map (old class to new class) honoured when a mission loads.
benefit: Mods can rename classes without breaking missions.

title: No formation-spacing control
limitation: No script command sets formation spacing: slots come from fixed tables scaled by `formationX/Z`; SAFE and CARELESS units ignore their slots and follow the previous unit in ID order; LIMITED caps the leader at 22 % outside COMBAT.
current_workaround: The staging planner computes predicted files and spacing; one group per vehicle for an open column.
proposed_feature: [command] A spacing (formation scale) setter per group.
benefit: Convoys and patrols that keep believable intervals.
